claim: Diabetes affects >10% of adults worldwide.
source: Diabetes affects >10% of adults worldwide and is caused by impaired production or response to insulin, resulting in chronic hyperglycemia.
evidence: This is a statement about diabetes prevalence that draws from established epidemiological knowledge.

claim: Diabetes is caused by impaired production or response to insulin, resulting in chronic hyperglycemia.
source: Diabetes affects >10% of adults worldwide and is caused by impaired production or response to insulin, resulting in chronic hyperglycemia.
evidence: This is a fundamental definition of diabetes based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Pancreatic islet β-cells are the sole source of endogenous insulin.
source: Pancreatic islet β-cells are the sole source of endogenous insulin, and our understanding of β-cell dysfunction and death in type 2 diabetes (T2D) is incomplete.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in diabetes biology.

claim: Our understanding of β-cell dysfunction and death in type 2 diabetes (T2D) is incomplete.
source: Pancreatic islet β-cells are the sole source of endogenous insulin, and our understanding of β-cell dysfunction and death in type 2 diabetes (T2D) is incomplete.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq data supports heterogeneity as an important factor in β-cell function and survival.
source: Single-cell RNA-seq data supports heterogeneity as an important factor in β-cell function and survival.
evidence: This statement references findings from single-cell RNA-seq studies in the field.

claim: DEGAS is a deep transfer learning tool that maps disease associations onto single-cell RNA-seq data from bulk expression data.
source: To address this, we applied a deep transfer learning tool, DEGAS, which maps disease associations onto single-cell RNA-seq data from bulk expression data.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Independent runs of DEGAS using T2D or obesity status identified distinct β-cell subpopulations.
source: Independent runs of DEGAS using T2D or obesity status identified distinct β-cell subpopulations.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's analysis.

claim: A singular cluster of T2D-associated β-cells was identified.
source: A singular cluster of T2D-associated β-cells was identified; however, β-cells with high obese-DEGAS scores contained two subpopulations derived largely from either non-diabetic (ND) or T2D donors.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the DEGAS analysis.

claim: β-cells with high obese-DEGAS scores contained two subpopulations derived largely from either non-diabetic (ND) or T2D donors.
source: A singular cluster of T2D-associated β-cells was identified; however, β-cells with high obese-DEGAS scores contained two subpopulations derived largely from either non-diabetic (ND) or T2D donors.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the DEGAS analysis.

claim: The obesity-associated ND cells were enriched for translation and unfolded protein response genes compared to T2D cells.
source: The obesity-associated ND cells were enriched for translation and unfolded protein response genes compared to T2D cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis of the DEGAS-identified subpopulations.

claim: CDKN1C was increased in β-cells from T2D donors, in agreement with the DEGAS predictions.
source: CDKN1C was increased in β-cells from T2D donors, in agreement with the DEGAS predictions, while DLK1 appeared depleted from T2D islets of some donors.
evidence: This is a validation finding from immunostaining experiments.

claim: DLK1 appeared depleted from T2D islets of some donors.
source: CDKN1C was increased in β-cells from T2D donors, in agreement with the DEGAS predictions, while DLK1 appeared depleted from T2D islets of some donors.
evidence: This is a validation finding from immunostaining experiments.

claim: Both CDKN1C and DLK1 were heterogeneously expressed among β-cells.
source: Both CDKN1C and DLK1 were heterogeneously expressed among β-cells.
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining experiments.

claim: scRNA-seq analysis has enabled identification of multiple reliable transcriptomic markers for endocrine and exocrine pancreatic cell types.
source: Notably, these studies have (1) identified multiple reliable transcriptomic markers for endocrine and exocrine pancreatic cell types; (2) provided insight into novel subtypes of cells; and (3) generated large cellular atlases spurring innovation in the development of single-cell methods and analysis.
evidence: This statement references findings from published scRNA-seq studies.

claim: scRNA-seq studies have provided insight into novel subtypes of cells.
source: Notably, these studies have (1) identified multiple reliable transcriptomic markers for endocrine and exocrine pancreatic cell types; (2) provided insight into novel subtypes of cells; and (3) generated large cellular atlases spurring innovation in the development of single-cell methods and analysis.
evidence: This statement references findings from published scRNA-seq studies.

claim: scRNA-seq studies have generated large cellular atlases spurring innovation in the development of single-cell methods and analysis.
source: Notably, these studies have (1) identified multiple reliable transcriptomic markers for endocrine and exocrine pancreatic cell types; (2) provided insight into novel subtypes of cells; and (3) generated large cellular atlases spurring innovation in the development of single-cell methods and analysis.
evidence: This statement references the impact of published scRNA-seq studies.

claim: scRNA-seq analysis has enabled a more robust characterization of islet cell heterogeneity, which may underlie diversity in diabetes risk and drug response.
source: scRNA-seq analysis has enabled a more robust characterization of islet cell heterogeneity, which may underlie diversity in diabetes risk and drug response (Baron et al., 2016; Li et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016; Lawlor et al., 2017; Fang et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Differences were observed in the relative proportion of major cell types between humans versus mice and pigs in islet single-cell transcriptomes.
source: In published comparisons between the islet single-cell transcriptomes of humans versus mice and pigs, differences were observed in the relative proportion of major cell types as well as in many cell type-specific genes (Tritschler et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a published comparative study.

claim: Differences were observed in many cell type-specific genes between humans versus mice and pigs in islet single-cell transcriptomes.
source: In published comparisons between the islet single-cell transcriptomes of humans versus mice and pigs, differences were observed in the relative proportion of major cell types as well as in many cell type-specific genes (Tritschler et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a published comparative study.

claim: Some sets of islet scRNA-seq data have been combined and made searchable through web portals to browse datasets and compare cell types and marker genes.
source: Some sets of islet scRNA-seq data have been combined and made searchable through web portals to browse datasets and compare cell types and marker genes (Tritschler et al., 2022; Segerstolpe et al., 2016; Mawla and Huising, 2019; Elgamal et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published resources.

claim: DEGAS was previously developed as a flexible deep transfer learning framework that can be used to overlay disease status, survival hazard, drug response, and other clinical information directly onto single cells.
source: To further utilize these types of integrated transcriptomic data and donor metadata, we previously developed DEGAS as a flexible deep transfer learning framework that can be used to overlay disease status, survival hazard, drug response, and other clinical information directly onto single cells.
evidence: This describes the prior development of the DEGAS tool by the authors.

claim: Machine learning tools like DEGAS have been primarily used in cancer datasets, but not in human pancreatic islets until now.
source: Machine learning tools like DEGAS have been primarily used in cancer datasets, but not in human pancreatic islets until now.
evidence: This statement describes the novelty of applying DEGAS to islet data.

claim: The reasons why some obese individuals succumb to T2D while others do not likely involve both genetic and environmental factors.
source: The reasons why some obese individuals succumb to T2D while others do not likely involve both genetic and environmental factors, but the factors that underlie this transition are incompletely understood (Fabbrini et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and represents current understanding in the field.

claim: The factors that underlie the transition from obesity to T2D are incompletely understood.
source: The reasons why some obese individuals succumb to T2D while others do not likely involve both genetic and environmental factors, but the factors that underlie this transition are incompletely understood (Fabbrini et al., 2015).

claim: Analyses of human genomics and islet transcriptomics indicate many β-cell genes have causal roles in T2D.

claim: The bulk RNA-seq data from Marselli et al., 2020 (GSE159984) contains 58 ND and 27 T2D samples with associated metadata for BMI, age, and sex.

claim: Altered expression of IAPP was observed in T2D human islets from the Marselli dataset.

claim: β-Cells had a wide distribution of T2D-DEGAS scores, possibly reflecting β-cell heterogeneity or altered β-cell gene expression after onset of T2D.
source: β-Cells had a wide distribution of scores, possibly reflecting β-cell heterogeneity or altered β-cell gene expression after onset of T2D (Figure 3B; Weir et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an observation from the DEGAS analysis with speculative interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: High-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells had elevated expression of CDKN1C.
source: High-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells had elevated expression of CDKN1C (p57Kip2) which binds and inhibits G1 cyclin/CDK complexes and is also involved in cellular senescence (Stampone et al., 2018; Ou et al., 2019), and reduced expression of IAPP, consistent with results from bulk T2D islet expression data (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis of DEGAS-identified subpopulations.

claim: CDKN1C (p57Kip2) binds and inhibits G1 cyclin/CDK complexes and is also involved in cellular senescence.
source: High-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells had elevated expression of CDKN1C (p57Kip2) which binds and inhibits G1 cyclin/CDK complexes and is also involved in cellular senescence (Stampone et al., 2018; Ou et al., 2019), and reduced expression of IAPP, consistent with results from bulk T2D islet expression data (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CDKN1C function supported by citations.

claim: High-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells had reduced expression of IAPP, consistent with results from bulk T2D islet expression data.
source: High-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells had elevated expression of CDKN1C (p57Kip2) which binds and inhibits G1 cyclin/CDK complexes and is also involved in cellular senescence (Stampone et al., 2018; Ou et al., 2019), and reduced expression of IAPP, consistent with results from bulk T2D islet expression data (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis of DEGAS-identified subpopulations.

claim: Over 90% of significant differentially expressed genes between high and low βT2D-DEGAS cells were only identified through DEGAS analysis and not by comparing all ND and T2D β-cells.
source: This process left over 90% of significant differentially expressed genes remaining which were only identified through DEGAS analysis (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding demonstrating the added value of DEGAS over simple comparisons.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) analysis on high-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells showed enrichment in biological process categories including neutrophil degranulation, cell growth, and negative regulation of cell development.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis on high-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells showed enrichment in biological process categories including neutrophil degranulation, cell growth, and negative regulation of cell development (Figure 4E, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis of DEGAS-identified subpopulations.

claim: GO analysis on low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells showed enrichment of categories primarily related to membrane protein targeting, translation, and mitochondrial electron transport.
source: Conversely, GO analysis on low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells showed enrichment of categories primarily related to membrane protein targeting, translation, and mitochondrial electron transport (Figure 4F, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis of DEGAS-identified subpopulations.

claim: The top six enriched GO categories in low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells were driven largely by RPS/RPL genes.
source: The top six enriched GO categories were driven largely by RPS/RPL genes.
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis.

claim: Ranked-list GSEA on high- versus low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS subpopulations largely agreed with the GO analysis.
source: We also performed ranked-list GSEA on these same high- versus low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS subpopulations, which largely agreed with the GO analysis (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a finding from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Significant positive enrichment for hypoxia, TNFα signaling, estrogen response, and glycolysis was observed in high-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells.
source: We observed significant positive enrichment for hypoxia, TNFα signaling, estrogen response, and glycolysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), while significant negative enriched pathways included overlapping genes in oxidative phosphorylation and Myc-target pathways (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Significant negative enriched pathways in low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells included overlapping genes in oxidative phosphorylation and Myc-target pathways.
source: We observed significant positive enrichment for hypoxia, TNFα signaling, estrogen response, and glycolysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), while significant negative enriched pathways included overlapping genes in oxidative phosphorylation and Myc-target pathways (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the GSEA analysis.

claim: The cell types with the highest obesity-association scores were β-cells, acinar cells, and stellate cells.
source: The cell types with the highest obesity-association scores were β-cells, acinar cells, and stellate cells (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from the obesity-DEGAS analysis.

claim: The subpopulation of βlean-DEGAS cells appears to overlap with the subpopulation of low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells.
source: It is notable that the subpopulation of βlean-DEGAS cells appears to overlap with the subpopulation of low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells, suggesting that single β-cells share features of low BMI and potentially lower T2D association.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the two DEGAS analyses.

claim: Two subpopulations of high-scoring βobese-DEGAS cells were observed.
source: However, we observed two subpopulations of high-scoring βobese-DEGAS cells (Figure 6A), a feature that did not occur with βT2D-DEGAS cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the obesity-DEGAS analysis.

claim: A distinguishing difference between the two groups of obesity-associated β-cells was the donor diabetes status (ND vs. T2D) from within the single-cell metadata.
source: We observed that a distinguishing difference between these two groups of obesity-associated β-cells was the donor diabetes status (ND vs. T2D) from within the single-cell metadata.
evidence: This is an observation from analyzing the obesity-DEGAS results.

claim: GO analysis of genes upregulated in the ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster indicated an enrichment for unfolded protein response (UPR) processes like vesicle transport, translation, and protein folding and stability.
source: GO analysis of genes upregulated in the ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster indicated an enrichment for unfolded protein response (UPR) processes like vesicle transport, translation, and protein folding and stability (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from the pathway analysis of obesity-DEGAS subpopulations.

claim: The ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster was enriched for expression of adaptive UPR genes (e.g. MANF and HSPA5) and maladaptive UPR genes (e.g. TRIB3 and DDIT3).
source: Specifically, the ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster was enriched for expression of adaptive (e.g. MANF and HSPA5) and maladaptive (e.g. TRIB3 and DDIT3) UPR genes, as well as genes involved in ER-associated degradation (e.g. SEL1L, DERL2, and SDF2L1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis of obesity-DEGAS subpopulations.

claim: The ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster was enriched for genes involved in ER-associated degradation (e.g. SEL1L, DERL2, and SDF2L1).
source: Specifically, the ND-βobese-DEGAS cluster was enriched for expression of adaptive (e.g. MANF and HSPA5) and maladaptive (e.g. TRIB3 and DDIT3) UPR genes, as well as genes involved in ER-associated degradation (e.g. SEL1L, DERL2, and SDF2L1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis of obesity-DEGAS subpopulations.

claim: GO analysis of genes upregulated in the T2D-βobese-DEGAS cluster showed enrichment for hormone transport and secretion pathways (e.g. IGFBP5, UCN3, G6PC2) and inflammatory/immune-related pathways (e.g. HLA-A/B/E, STAT3).

evidence: This is a finding from the GSEA analysis.

claim: DLK1 and CDKN1C ranked highly in both T2D-DEGAS and obese-DEGAS analyses.

claim: DLK1 expression overlapped with T2D-βobese-DEGAS cells.

claim: CDKN1C expression overlapped with high-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells.

claim: CDKN1C expression overlapped with T2D-βobese-DEGAS cells.

claim: CDKN1C staining was primarily nuclear and was heterogeneous across β-cells in ND human pancreas.

claim: DEGAS allows the definition of essentially new cell subpopulations that would not necessarily be identified by standard clustering algorithms.
source: Notably, this direct transfer to single cells avoids the cluster resolution problems that arise using deconvolution approaches, allowing for subsets of cells within a cluster to be assigned different associations with clinical outcomes. In this way, DEGAS allows the definition of essentially new cell subpopulations that would not necessarily be identified by standard clustering algorithms, and these subpopulations are rationally selected based on assigned disease-association scores.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the DEGAS method.

claim: The disease-associated single cells identified by DEGAS are those cells whose transcriptomic signature shares complex patterns with patient transcriptomics that have known clinical and metabolic attributes.
source: A key point from our study is that the disease-associated single cells identified by DEGAS are those cells whose transcriptomic signature shares complex patterns with patient transcriptomics that have known clinical and metabolic attributes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of how DEGAS works.

claim: The major advantages of DEGAS are (1) the ability to select subsets of β-cells at an individual cell resolution based on their disease association; (2) unique qualities of the highly non-linear DEGAS technology versus linear models of other tools to detect complex molecular programs; and (3) speed and scalability based on efficient implementation.
source: The major advantages of DEGAS are (1) the ability to select subsets of β-cells at an individual cell resolution based on their disease association; (2) unique qualities of the highly non-linear DEGAS technology versus linear models of other tools to detect complex molecular programs; and (3) speed and scalability based on efficient implementation.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of DEGAS compared to other methods.

claim: DEGAS has the potential to be used on datasets containing well over 1 million cells, unlike other methods.
source: DEGAS has the potential to be used on datasets containing well over 1 million cells, unlike other methods.
evidence: This is a statement about the scalability of DEGAS.

claim: RePACT has successfully uncovered genes associated with β-cell heterogeneity in T2D and obesity.

source: Downregulation of HNF1A in T2D β-cells, and reduced FXYD2 expression as a result, may contribute to membrane hyperpolarization and reduced function (Weng et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

source: BTG1 and BTG2 are known as anti-proliferation factors.

claim: RPS/RPL ribosomal genes are known to be highly expressed in primary human β-cells.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells may have relatively increased translation and metabolic activity.

source: Taken together, high-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells may be reflective of dysfunctional β-cells in either a pre-T2D or T2D-onset state, while low-scoring βT2D-DEGAS cells could potentially represent more resilient β-cells.
